cards.text: Elihu, the young man who waited his turn to speak (Job 32:4, 6), has been talking to Job (Job 33:1). Now he keeps going and turns to a new crowd: wise men, men of learning. Baker, this man waited a LONG time for the floor, and he is NOT giving it back.

cards.question: Elihu wants the wise men to give his words a real test. He says the ear tests words the way the mouth does what?
True or false: Elihu tells the wise men to sort out what is right on their own, without him.

cards.text: Now Elihu brings up Job by name and quotes what he says Job has declared. Baker, NOBODY likes hearing their own words read back in front of a crowd.

cards.question: What does Elihu say Job has declared?

answers.text: He is righteous but God denied him justice
He sinned and earned all his suffering
His friends are the ones who wronged him

cards.text: Elihu's not done with the quotes, friend. He keeps going: 'Would I lie about my case? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.'
Then Elihu asks, 'What man is like Job, who drinks up derision like water?' Baker, that is NOT a compliment you frame and hang up in the bakery.

cards.question: Elihu isn't finished with Job yet. Who does Elihu say Job keeps company with?
According to Elihu, Job has said a man gets no profit from delighting in ___.

cards.text: So Elihu calls the men of understanding to listen up. Friend, THIS is the batch he's been preheating the oven for.

cards.question: Elihu says something is far from God and the Almighty. What is it?

answers.text: Hearing the cry of the poor

cards.question: Elihu says God repays a man according to his ___.

cards.text: Elihu says it AGAIN, like a man who just found his caps lock key: God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice. Then he asks who gave God charge over the earth, and who appointed Him over the whole world.

cards.question: True or false: Elihu says that if God withdrew His Spirit and breath, all flesh would perish together.

cards.text: Elihu says, 'If you have understanding, hear this; listen to my words.' That's three times now he's told folks to listen, baker, and I'm starting to think he MEANS it.
Then he asks two big questions: could one who hates justice govern, and will the listener condemn the just and mighty One?

cards.question: True or false: Elihu says the just and mighty One goes easy on kings and nobles.
Elihu says God is not partial to princes and does not favor the rich over the poor. Why not?

answers.text: They are all the work of His hands
The poor pray more often than the rich
Riches never last for very long

cards.text: Elihu says they die in an instant, in the middle of the night, and the mighty are removed without human hand, for God sees a man's every step. EVERY step, baker? I hop around on this gold base, and I bet He's counting every single hop.

cards.question: True or false: Elihu says the workers of iniquity can still hide from God in deep darkness.

cards.text: Elihu says God doesn't need to examine a man any further or bring him in for judgment. No hearing, no meeting, no 'let's circle back next week': He shatters the mighty without inquiry.

cards.question: When God shatters the mighty, what else does Elihu say He does?

answers.text: Sets up others in their place
Hands their power to the poor

cards.text: Elihu says God recognizes their deeds and overthrows them in the night. And He strikes them for their wickedness in full view, baker, out in the open where EVERYBODY can see it.

cards.question: Elihu says God strikes the mighty for their wickedness. What reason does Elihu give?

answers.text: They grew too rich and proud

cards.question: Elihu says the ones God strikes caused the cry of the ___ to come before Him, and He heard it.

cards.text: Then Elihu asks two questions, and friend, let them sit a second: 'But when He remains silent, who can condemn Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him?'

cards.question: Even when God remains silent, what does Elihu say He still does?

answers.text: Rests from all of His work
Leaves the world to its kings

cards.question: True or false: Elihu says God watches over man and nation so that godless men should not rule.

cards.text: Now Elihu paints a picture, baker. 'Suppose someone says to God, 'I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more. Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.''
Then Elihu asks, 'Should God repay you on your own terms when you have disavowed Him?' I bet THAT one made everybody listening go real quiet.

cards.question: True or false: Elihu says a choice has to be made here, and that he is the one who will make it.
Elihu says the wise men who hear him will speak up about Job. What does Elihu say they will say?

answers.text: Job has been wronged by God
Job is wiser than all of them

cards.text: Then Elihu says, 'If only Job were tried to the utmost for answering like a wicked man.' Oof. If words were ovens, baker, Elihu just cranked his all the way to broil.

cards.question: Elihu wraps up his complaint about Job. He says Job multiplies his words against ___.

cards.text: Elihu says Job adds rebellion to his sin and claps his hands among them. And that's where we set the timer down for now, friend, because this story is far from finished.
